learning_outcomes.text: Explain and interpret the main statistical concepts.
Use descriptive statistics tools to analyse sample or populational data.
Use excel spreadsheets to solve descriptive statistics problems.
Solve common problems involving basic theory of probability, random variables, probability distributions, random sampling, confidence intervals, hypothesis testing and ANOVA.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Statistics: Scope and method
Descriptive statistics: Description of univariate and bivariate samples of quantitative or qualitative data
Random variables and probability distributions: distributions of discrete and continuous variables, distribution parameters transformed variables
Joint distribution of two random variables: joint, marginal and conditional distributions, independent variables, covariance and correlation, distribution of functions of two variables
Probability distributions of discrete random variables: the Binomial distribution, the Hypergeometric distribution and the Poisson distribution

Probability distributions of continuous random variables: the Uniform distribution, the Negative exponential distribution, and the Normal distribution, the t distribution, the Chi-square distribution and the F distribution
Random sampling and sampling distributions: distribution of the sample mean. the Central limit theorem, Generation of random smaples
assessment_rules: The final classification (CF) is obtained by the formula CF = 0.25 ME + 0.75 E, where ME is a mini-exam and E is the final exam. To pass the course, students must achieve a minimum of 7 points on the final exam (E). The mini-exam cannot be repeated, but global improvement is possible only through a new comprehensive exam covering all syllabus content, with a weight of 0.75. Students must meet minimum attendance requirements to be admitted to exams, as per FEUP's student evaluation regulations.
